mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Friday, October 23, 2026. Amazon Web Services has introduced a new approach to training artificial intelligence agents using Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI. Unlike standard fine-tuning, which focuses on single prompts, this method is designed for agentic tasks—such as filing expense reports or triaging support tickets—that require a sequence of dependent actions where only the final outcome can be objectively measured. By using a reward-based system, developers can train smaller, cost-effective models to perform specific business workflows. In a test case using the game Wordle, researchers reported increasing the solve rate of a 20-billion parameter model from 15 percent to 69 percent at low reasoning settings. The system architecture involves SageMaker AI managing the training job while Amazon Bedrock AgentCore hosts the agent and environment. AWS noted that datasets and models remain within the user's account and are not utilized for base model training. In major infrastructure news, OpenAI has detailed its ongoing transition to a multi-tenant storage architecture to support over one billion ChatGPT users. In the second part of a technical report, the company described how it optimized Azure Cosmos DB to manage 500 petabytes of data across 40 geographic regions. OpenAI shifted from single-tenant containers—where each product team managed its own database—to a centralized multi-tenant approach. This move aimed to reduce the costs and inefficiencies associated with over-provisioning resources. While multi-tenancy introduces risks like noisy neighbors—where one application consumes disproportionate resources—OpenAI stated that it leverages built-in Azure primitives to mitigate these issues while maintaining millisecond-level response times. In Kazakhstan, the domestic AI ecosystem is expanding through new partnerships and infrastructure projects. During a visit to Astana, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang met with government officials to discuss the nation’s goal of building homegrown artificial intelligence, specifically models capable of processing the Kazakh language and cultural context. As part of this push, the company Firebird has secured an export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell graphics processing units, which will be housed in a new facility under construction with Kazakhtelecom. Additionally, the ride-hailing company inDrive announced it has signed an agreement with Pony.ai and NVIDIA to begin testing robotaxis in Astana in 2027. The project aims to evaluate autonomous driving technology in challenging winter weather conditions, with plans to initially operate vehicles with safety operators on board. In research and developer news, Hugging Face has unveiled LitPivot, a system designed to help researchers navigate the process of refining ideas based on academic literature. The tool allows users to segment research proposals into specific facets—such as the problem statement or evaluation plan—and then provides critiques supported by relevant research papers. In a study involving 17 researchers, participants reported that ideas developed with LitPivot were better grounded in existing literature compared to those developed using standard text editors. Meanwhile, Microsoft Research has introduced Flint-interactive, a new language that allows AI agents to create complex, interactive data visualizations. By using a compiler to handle interaction logic, the system enables users to click, zoom, and filter data within charts without requiring the agent to write low-level rendering code. Regarding security and industry standards, the certificate authority eMudhra has announced its exit from the Transport Layer Security (TLS) business. This decision follows independent reporting earlier this week that the company had issued eight credentials with extremely weak private keys. Some of these keys were as short as four bits, making them trivial to compromise. The company stated that the scrutiny surrounding the incident was disproportionate to the business’s revenue from this sector, which accounted for only one percent of its total earnings.
